title: SEBI Allows Mutual Fund Schemes to Net Settle Cash Market Trades From April 2027
seo_title: SEBI's New Mutual Fund Net Settlement Rule
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India
case_name: SEBI Circular on the Framework for Net Settlement of Funds for Mutual Fund Scheme Transactions in the Cash Market
card_summary: SEBI's circular of 5 November 2026 lets a mutual fund scheme net its fund pay-in and pay-out for outright cash market trades within the same settlement cycle, effective 1 April 2027. Only the money leg nets; securities still settle gross, and a scheme that both buys and sells the same security in a cycle cannot use this. SEBI had already given foreign portfolio investors this option in April 2026.
card_tip: AMCs should confirm system readiness with custodians well before 1 April 2027, since trustees must review the netting process first, and it will not help a scheme that both buys and sells the same security in a cycle.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: HNI investors in mutual fund schemes who benefit from lower scheme-level funding costs and steadier NAV computation, with a secondary domestic angle for AMCs and custodians implementing the change. TARGET QUERY: what is SEBI's new net settlement rule for mutual funds. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen. Cross-verified from Moneylife, LiveLawBiz and Cafemutual, which agree the circular issued 5 November 2026 permits netting of the money leg only, at individual scheme level, for outright cash-market purchases and sales within the same settlement cycle, effective 1 April 2027, excludes a scheme that both buys and sells the same security in a cycle, and follows a similar framework SEBI gave foreign portfolio investors in April 2026 after a September 2026 consultation paper. The circular number is given by secondary reports as HO/24/13(1)2026-IMD-POD-2/I/25242/2026; the SEBI circular PDF itself was not opened directly in this run, so the exact circular number should be checked against sebi.gov.in before publication.
